newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar soars, European stocks mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar soars, European stocks mixed.

text.p: The dollar surged on Monday, climbing to a four-year high against the Swiss franc, an eight-year peak against the French franc and mark and nearly a 12-year high against the lira on nervousness over German interest rates.
Interest rate jitters, coupled with corporate earnings, also kept European stocks mixed at midday.

The dollar posted its biggest gains against the lira, which slid to the lowest level versus the dollar since late 1985, as Italian government debt prices fell relative to German government debt prices, said Chris Furness, analyst at 4Cast.
Furness noted the same trend in Swedish markets on Monday. As Swedish debt prices fell, the dollar scored about a 3-1/2 year high against the Swedish crown.
The dollar's rise was also spurred by fears Germany's central bank would raise interest rates via its weekly repurchase rate tender, or money market operation.

Before the Bundesbank left for its four-week summer recess, it said it would hold 3.0-percent fixed-rate tenders for two weeks. By not specifying the rates for the final two weeks of the holiday period, traders speculated the central bank might use a variable rate tender to allow rates to drift higher.

Though higher interest rates are normally supportive for a currency, traders feared higher interest rates in this instance would further stifle already weak economic growth and dent the Bundesbank's credibility.
"...the question is how credible is such a move when domestic demand is relatively weak," said Mark Geddes, treasury economist at ABN Amro.
Because of the ongoing debate about German interest rates, traders were not ready to sell marks without more clues on Bundesbank interest rate policy. So instead, they bought dollars.
Uncertainty about Bundesbank policy also rattled Germany's blue-chip DAX index. The DAX ended bourse trade down 111.85 points, or more than 2.50 percent, at 4,296.94.

Bank shares led the declines. Commerzbank AG was down 1.15 marks at 61.50, Deutsche Bank AG down 4.75 at 117.40, Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG down 3.90 at 72.05 and Bay Vereinsbank was down 3.00 at 95.80.
London's FTSE-100 index cut losses after HSBC Holdings Plc soared to a year high of 2,326 pence on better-than-expected first-half results.

The bank said pre-tax profits in sterling terms rose 13 percent to 2.623 billion pounds ($4.3 billion), with dividends up 33 percent to 20 pence per share. That compares with analysts' forecasts for pre-tax profits between 2.32 and 2.48 billion pounds.
But FTSE activity was expected to be limited with interest rate worries looming. The Bank of England's monetary policy-setting meeting is on Wednesday and Thursday.
A Reuters poll taken on July 30 showed 16 of 23 economists expected official British interest rates to rise 25 basis points after the meeting for the fourth rate rise in so many months.
French shares were also weaker, but traders expected losses to be limited by the dollar's strength.
Finland's FOX index gave up early gains to edge lower, but activity was modest as traders awaited Nokia Ab, Oy's second-quarter report at 1300 GMT.

The mobile phone maker was expected to post impressive earnings after Ericsson posted better-than-expected results more than a week ago. Analysts forecast Nokia's second-quarter pre-tax profits at 1.64 billion markka ($295.4 million), up from 728 million a year ago.
But one broker said "I think it would have to be 1.7 to 1.8 billion to justify this (Nokia's share) price."
Nokia shares hit a year high of 485 markka in early trade, and the FOX index was down 0.61 point at 1,237.57 in early afternoon.
Dutch stocks also rose in anticipation of second-quarter results from several blue-chip companies.

Steel and aluminium group Koninklijke Nederlandsche Hoogovens en Staalfabrieken NV shares jumped to a year high of 139.80 guilders ($66.59) on expectations of solid earnings growth when it reports on Wednesday.
"We're not negative on those figures and neither is the market," a dealer said, adding that the shares should also benefit because it is a cyclical stock.
CURRENCIES AT 1240 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8677 marks and 118.55 yen compared to 1.8630 and 118.37 in late trading on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1240 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 7.8 points at 4,891.50.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index ended bourse trade down 111.85 points at 4,296.94. The DAX IBIS index was down 47.59 points at 4,289.39 in electronic trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 45.52 points at 3,003.92.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at 1030 in London at $324.05, down from Friday's close at $324.25.
